object_description: diamond-shaped solitary building with stepped forecourt
design_condition: The solitary building occupies the southern site, follows the track field, forms a triangular forecourt toward the boulevard, and leaves the northern site as a campus park with connections beneath the viaduct.

positive.statement: The building acts convincingly as a space-defining urban element and a large solitary form.

position.rationale: Diamond massing and solitary footprint are visible across the calibrated top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The compact shape creates a large, well-positioned open space with varied usability.

position.rationale: The triangular stepped forecourt is clearly visible along the building’s southern edge.

positive.statement: The high-quality open-space design provides attractive and versatile urban landscapes.

position.rationale: The northern open site is the clearest sampled location for the campus park landscape.

positive.statement: The clear spatial organization is flexible and independent across the floors.

position.rationale: Upper-level organization is constrained to the stepped multi-storey mass visible in elevations.

positive.statement: The single-house solution and north-facing central infrastructure areas are operationally convincing.

position.rationale: The north-facing band is identifiable directionally, though infrastructure rooms are not separately visible.

positive.statement: The compact structure promises economical and sustainable construction.

position.rationale: This is a performance judgment without a specific spatial referent.

negative.statement: The building lacks options for identifying the individual departments.

position.rationale: Interior departmental identity is not distinguishable; the central upper mass provides a constrained surface anchor.

negative.statement: The compact solitaire produces excessive internal density.

position.rationale: Density criticism applies to the compact central building mass visible throughout the sampled model.

negative.statement: The missing entrance on the viaduct side weakens access from public transport.

position.rationale: The viaduct-side entrance is constrained to the northern perimeter, where no distinct opening appears.

negative.statement: The upper floors have narrow internal corridors and limited daylight areas.

position.rationale: Upper-floor circulation and daylight conditions are not resolved internally, so the upper mass is used.

negative.statement: Strategic open spaces and the foyer situation for publicly accessed classrooms are not optimally solved.

position.target: public classroom foyer and strategic open spaces
position.rationale: The public-facing foyer and adjacent open-space issue are anchored near the southern forecourt.

negative.statement: The proposed timber-system structural grid is unsuitable in parts of the upper floors.

position.rationale: The structural grid is not individually visible; the upper-floor structure receives a constrained mass anchor.

negative.statement: The large glazing still creates a risk of overheating and deep rooms strain daylight conditions.

position.rationale: Glazing is not distinguishable, so the exposed east-south envelope anchors overheating and daylight concerns.
